title: Google Flights Prices

routes.title: Routes
routes.description: Routes as airport codes, e.g. ["JFK-LHR", "LIS-CDG"]; written "LIS-LHR", "lis > lhr" or "JFK to LAX". Google city codes work too: "NYC-LON" searches every New York and London airport. Required, with departDate. Every route is searched for every date, so 3 routes with sweepDays 6 = 21 searches of about 10 to 35 billed itineraries each. Same origin and destination, or a code that is not three letters, is refused before anything is charged.
routes.sectionDescription: Routes and a departure date; add a return date for round trips.

departDate.title: Departure date
departDate.description: Departure date: "2026-11-20" (YYYY-MM-DD), or relative to the day the run starts: "30 days", "6 weeks", "tomorrow". Use relative dates for scheduled runs ("track this fare daily"): the input never needs editing and always looks the same distance ahead. Required. A past date is refused before anything is charged.

returnDate.title: Return date
returnDate.description: Empty (default) = one-way fares. A date = round trip: "2026-11-27", or relative "37 days". Every row then prices the outbound with its return, and price is the total for both legs (round_trip_total true). Use for "round trip flight prices". Must be on or after departDate.

sweepDays.title: Also price the next N departure days
sweepDays.description: 0 (default) = only the departure date above. N = the same trip also departing on each of the next N days, e.g. departDate "30 days", sweepDays 6 = 7 departure days = 7 searches per route; a returnDate shifts with each day so the trip length stays. Use for a price calendar or "which day is cheapest": sort flight rows by price, or read `cheapest` on each status row. Cost multiplies by N + 1; cap it with maxResultsPerSearch. Maximum 60. One row per day instead: kestrel/flight-price-tracker.
sweepDays.sectionDescription: More departure days per route, and the cap on rows per search that decides the bill.

maxResultsPerSearch.title: Max itineraries per search
maxResultsPerSearch.description: 0 (default) = every itinerary Google lists for a route and date, usually 10 to 35 rows at $0.005 each. N = only the first N in Google's own order (its "best" ranking, not strictly the cheapest), e.g. 5: the main cost cap, at most N × $0.005 per route and date. Use 1 to 5 for "the cheapest fare" or "a few options", 0 for the whole market. Maximum 200.

seat.title: Cabin
seat.description: Cabin: "economy" (default), "premium_economy", "business" or "first". Business and first class fares are a different, smaller set of itineraries than economy, usually fewer rows. Use "business" for "business class fares".
seat.sectionDescription: Each of these changes the fares Google returns.

maxStops.title: Stops
maxStops.description: "any" (default) = every itinerary Google lists. "nonstop" = nonstop flights only; "one_or_fewer"; "two_or_fewer". Google applies it before the results are listed, so nonstop-only returns fewer rows and costs less. Use "nonstop" for "direct flights only".

adults.title: Adults
adults.description: Adult passengers, 1 to 9, e.g. 2 (default 1). Every price is the total for all passengers on the row, not per person. Adults + children + infants is at most 9.

children.title: Children (2-11)
children.description: Children aged 2 to 11 in their own seat, 0 to 8, e.g. 2 (default 0). Prices include them. For "flight prices for a family of four" pass adults 2, children 2.

infantsSeat.title: Infants in seat
infantsSeat.description: Infants under 2 in their own seat, 0 to 8, e.g. 1 (default 0). Prices include them.

infantsLap.title: Infants on lap
infantsLap.description: Infants under 2 on an adult's lap, 0 to 8, e.g. 1 (default 0); at most one per adult. Prices include them.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: ISO 4217 code for every price, e.g. "EUR" (default "USD"). When the user names no currency, pass the one their market uses. A search Google prices in another currency (some markets ignore the request) is reported as an error on its status row and never billed in the wrong currency.
currency.sectionDescription: The two inputs that change the prices themselves.

market.title: Market (country)
market.description: Google market (gl) as a 2-letter country code, e.g. "de", "gb", "in" (default "us"). It is the country of the person searching, not the destination: fares, airlines and the currency Google accepts differ by market. Keep "us" unless the user wants fares as seen from a country. Results are read in English whatever the market (there is no language input).

sessions.title: Parallel sessions
sessions.description: Parallel proxy sessions (one egress IP each), 1 to 16, e.g. 4 (default 4). More = faster; each is paced separately. Leave at 4 unless a run is throttled.
sessions.sectionDescription: Leave these alone unless a run is being throttled.

perIp.title: Requests per second per IP
perIp.description: Requests per second per session, 0.1 to 2, e.g. 0.5 (default 0.5). Google tolerates about 0.5 per second per IP; raising it causes retries, not speed.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description: Apify Proxy, required: Google blocks datacentre traffic that is not rotated. The default (Apify Proxy, automatic group) works; leave it.

description: Google Flights prices. Minimal input: {"routes": ["LIS-LHR"], "departDate": "30 days"}; routes and departDate are both required. maxResultsPerSearch defaults to 0 = every itinerary Google lists, usually 10 to 35 rows per route and date at $0.005 each: set 5 for "the cheapest few", and remember sweepDays multiplies the searches.
